cadence: Weekly news picks, refreshed every Monday alongside citation rankings.
selection: The top stories from the trailing 30 days, scored on publisher authority, discussion volume, whether a concrete verifiable result is reported, whether it changes what agent builders do now, whether an artifact was released, and expected durability. Only primary sources are cited, and performance claims remain attributed to their publishers.

items.title: GLM-Legal: Advancing Agentic Legal Intelligence
items.why: Z.ai introduces a GLM-5.3-Flash-based legal specialist and describes joint optimization of model training and the agent harness. It reports a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey LAB, 12.5 points above its base model; beta participation is invited and AutoClaw integration is forthcoming.

items.title: Proactive Agentic Orchestration
items.why: The authors release POrchestra, allowing sub-agents to request harness adjustments during execution, and OPOD, which distills hindsight feedback into orchestration training. Across three long-horizon benchmarks, they report average relative success gains of 9.1% over the strongest orchestration baseline and 10.0% over existing small-orchestrator training baselines.

items.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks
items.why: The authors keep the LLM fixed while revising persistent natural-language world models, compiling them into code and verifying observed transitions. They report clearing all levels of 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games with mean RHAE 100.0 using 44% of the human action count.

items.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5
items.why: Anthropic releases Haiku 5.5 for compaction, summarization and subagent work, reporting 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. It estimates typical task costs around 75% below Haiku 4.5 and introduces adjustable effort for the Haiku tier.

items.title: Introducing Mistral Large 4
items.why: Mistral opens the public preview API for a one-trillion-parameter native multimodal flagship and reports 93.3% attack resistance on Lakera B3. The announcement promises weights by the end of October; this edition does not treat those weights as already released.

items.title: Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild
items.why: The authors introduce HarnessTester, which generates tests grounded in agent-harness contracts. They report detecting 122 real-world harness bugs, including 88 previously unknown bugs and 69 confirmed by developers, alongside larger coverage and mutation-score gains than general-purpose test generators.

items.title: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution
items.why: The authors combine modular harness reuse with bandit-guided compositional search while fixing model weights. Under matched candidate-evaluation budgets, they report gains of 2.00 to 7.01 points over Meta-Harness across four domains and 14.6% lower total cost including search.

items.title: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover
items.why: In a controlled authorization testbed, the authors find that stale scores preserve unsafe agents in 22 of 48 framework histories after requirements change. Full validation and validated rollback yield fully correct programs in the core study while retaining over 43% deployment savings.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
items.why: OpenAI reports a 6.4-point DeepSWE v1.1 gain over GPT-6 Sol at lower reasoning effort and cost, and seven points on OSWorld 2.0 offline at maximum effort. On Terminal-Bench Science 0.1, it reports an average cost of $5.47 per task at maximum effort versus $23.80 for Astra.

items.title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
items.why: The authors release SoL-Pi after auto-research selects reusable mechanisms for execution, compaction, observations and delegated reading. On 51 EdgeBench tasks with two model backbones, they report performance comparable to Pi while reducing recorded token traffic by 44.7-49.0% and API cost by about one third.
